1051: If you meet people who are right to ask, you may ask them for help. If they hide what they have and say no, the blame is theirs, not yours.
1052: Even asking for help can be a pleasure, if what you ask for comes to you without pain for either person.
1053: Asking can even have a kind of beauty, when you stand before people who hide nothing in their hearts and know what they should do.
1054: Asking people who would never hold back, not even in a dream, is as worthy of respect as giving.
1055: Some people are willing to stand before others and ask for help only because the world has people who never hold back when asked.
1056: Just seeing people who never hide what they have is enough to make all the pains of being poor go away at once.
1057: When someone who asks meets givers who give without looking down on them or mocking them, their heart is filled with deep joy.
1058: If there were no people who ask for help, all the coming and going in this cool, wide world would be like wooden puppets moving back and forth.
1059: If no one wanted to ask and receive, what fame or honor could givers ever have?
1060: A person who asks should not get angry when refused. The pain of their own need is proof enough of how things stand.
1061: Even when there are people as dear as your own eyes who would gladly give without hiding anything, never asking them at all is worth ten million times more.
1062: If the maker of the world meant some people to live by begging, then let that maker also wander about like a beggar and die.
1063: There is no harder, more foolish idea than the bold thought that you can end the pain of being poor by begging instead of working.
1064: A person who refuses to beg, even when they have nothing to live on, has a greatness so big that the whole world cannot hold it.
1065: Even if it is only rice porridge as thin as clear water, nothing is sweeter than food you have earned with your own hard work.
1066: Even if you are only asking for water for a thirsty cow, nothing brings more shame to your tongue than asking.
1067: I beg all people who beg for just one thing: if you must ask, never ask people who hide what they have.
1068: Begging is like a small boat with no protection. When it hits the rock of someone saying no, it breaks apart.
1069: The heart melts just thinking about begging. When it thinks of people who hide what they have and refuse, even that melted heart is destroyed.
1070: The life of a beggar leaves them the moment they hear 'no.' So where does the life of the person who says 'no' hide itself?
1071: Low, mean people look exactly like human beings. I have never seen any two other things look so much alike.
1072: Mean people are luckier than those who know what is good, because no worry ever troubles their hearts.
1073: Mean people are like the gods, because they too do whatever they please.
1074: When mean people meet others who behave even worse than they do, they puff up with pride at being better.
1075: Fear is the main reason mean people behave well. Other than that, they behave a little well only when they want something.
1076: Mean people are like a drum beaten to announce news, because they carry every secret they hear straight to others.
1077: After eating, mean people will not even shake the leftover grains off their wet hand for anyone, except for those who would punch them in the jaw with a fist.
1078: Good people help you as soon as you tell them your need. Mean people are like sugarcane: they give their juice only when they are crushed.
1079: When mean people see others wearing nice clothes and eating good food, they become experts at finding faults in them.
1080: What are mean people good for? When trouble comes, they rush to sell themselves, and that is all they are fit for.
1081: Is she a goddess, a rare peacock, or a human girl wearing heavy earrings? My heart is confused and cannot tell.
1082: When she looks back at me, her look is like a goddess who attacks and brings a whole army with her.
1083: I never knew before what people call Death. Now I know it: it has a lovely woman's form and big eyes that fight.
1084: This gentle, innocent girl has eyes that seem to drink the life of anyone who sees them. Her eyes do not match her soft nature.
1085: Is it Death, is it an eye, or is it a shy female deer? This young girl's look has all three in it at once.
1086: If her curved eyebrows would only stay straight and shade her eyes, her eyes would not make me tremble and suffer like this.
1087: The cloth over the young woman's chest is like the cloth placed over the eyes of a wild, angry elephant. It holds back a dangerous power.
1088: Oh no! My strength, which made even my enemies shake on the battlefield, has broken in front of her shining forehead alone.
1089: She already has the gentle look of a deer and a natural shyness. What use are other jewels, which are not part of her, on a girl like her?
1090: Strong drink brings joy only to those who drink it. Love is different, because it brings joy even to those who only look.
1091: Her dark-lined eyes have two kinds of look. One look gives me the ache of love, and the other is the cure for that ache.
1092: The quick look she steals at me when I am not looking is not just half of love's joy. It is more than half.
1093: She looked at me, and after looking, she lowered her head. That was like water poured on the growing plant of our love.
1094: When I look at her, she looks at the ground. When I do not look, she looks at me and smiles softly to herself.
1095: She does not look straight at me. Yet she glances sideways, as if narrowing one eye, and smiles to herself.
1096: Even when people who feel no anger speak as if they were strangers, the true meaning of their words is quickly understood.
1097: Small sharp words that hold no anger, and looks that seem unfriendly, are signs of people who love each other while acting like strangers.
1098: When I look at her, pleading, she softens and smiles gently. At that moment this delicate girl looks especially lovely.
1099: Looking at each other with a plain, ordinary look, as if they were strangers, is a habit found only among people in love.
1100: When eyes meet eyes and the looks agree, the words of the mouth are no use at all.
1101: All the joys of the five senses, seeing, hearing, tasting, smelling and touching, are found together in this one woman with bright bangles.
1102: For other illnesses, the medicine is something different from the illness. But for the love-sickness this jeweled girl causes, she herself is the only medicine.
1103: Can the heaven of the lotus-eyed god (the god whose eyes are like lotus flowers) be any sweeter than sleeping on the soft shoulder of the one you love?
1104: If I move away it burns me, and if I come near it cools me. Where did she get such a strange fire?
1105: Holding the girl whose hair is full of flowers brings joy, just as each thing you long for does at the very moment you want it.
1106: Every time I hold her, my drooping life grows fresh shoots again. This innocent girl's shoulders must be made of amrita (the drink that makes gods live forever).
1107: Holding this lovely, fair young woman feels like living in your own home and eating food you earned yourself, after sharing it with others.
1108: Sweet to two people in love is a hug so close that not even a breath of wind can pass between them.
1109: A small lovers' quarrel, making up, and coming close again: these are the rewards enjoyed by people whose love has come true.
1110: The more you learn, the more you find out how much you do not know. In the same way, each time I come close to my jeweled love, my love finds something new.
1111: Bless you, anicham flower (a flower so delicate it wilts if you just smell it), you are truly soft. But the one I love is even more delicate than you.
1112: My heart, you get dizzy whenever you see flowers, thinking her eyes are like these flowers that anyone can look at. But they are not.
1113: Her shoulders are like bamboo. Her skin is the color of young leaves, her smile is like pearls, she smells sweet, and her dark-lined eyes are as sharp as spears.
1114: If the blue water lilies could see her, they would hang their heads and stare at the ground, saying, 'We cannot match the eyes of this beautifully dressed girl.'
1115: She has put anicham flowers (very light, delicate flowers) in her hair without taking off their stems. Their weight will break her slender waist, and no happy drums will play now.
1116: The stars cannot tell the moon apart from this young woman's face, so they are confused and wander from their places.
1117: The bright moon grows full again after shrinking, yet it has a dark spot. Is there any such mark on this woman's face?
1118: Long live the moon! If you could shine like this woman's face, you would win my love too.
1119: Moon, if you want to be like the face of the girl whose eyes are like flowers, do not show yourself where everyone can see you.
1120: Even the anicham flower (a flower so soft it wilts at a touch) and a swan's soft feathers feel like prickly thorn burrs to this woman's feet.
1121: The wetness on the white teeth of this softly speaking girl is like milk and honey mixed together.
1122: Whatever the bond is between the body and the life inside it, that is the bond between this young woman and me.
1123: Little image in the pupil (the dark center) of my eye, go away! There is no room in there for the girl with the lovely forehead whom I love.
1124: When my jeweled love is with me, she is like life to my soul. When she leaves, she is like death to it.
1125: If I ever forgot the good qualities of the girl with bright, fighting eyes, I could remember them. But I never forget them at all.
1126: My lover never leaves my eyes. Even when I blink, he is not hurt, because he is so fine and delicate.
1127: Because my lover lives in my eyes, I do not even put kohl (dark eyeliner) on them, knowing it would hide him.
1128: Because my lover lives in my heart, I am afraid to eat anything hot, knowing it would burn him.
1129: I know that if I blink he will be hidden, so I keep my eyes open. For that reason alone, this town calls him unloving.
1130: He always lives happily in my heart, yet this town says he lives far away and does not love me.
1131: For those who have known love and now suffer without it, there is no help and no strength left except the madal. That is a horse of palm stems that a refused lover rides in public.
1132: My body and my life cannot bear this any longer. They have put shame aside and are ready to ride the madal (the palm-stem horse of a refused lover).
1133: Once I had shyness and a man's honor. Today all I have is the palm-stem horse that lovesick men ride.
1134: The wild flood of love sweeps away the raft made of shyness and a man's honor.
1135: The girl who wears small bangles strung like a garland has given me both the palm-stem horse and the sadness that hurts me every evening.
1136: Even at midnight I think about riding the palm-stem horse, since that innocent girl keeps my eyes from closing in sleep.
1137: There is nothing nobler than a woman who suffers a love as big as the sea and still never rides the palm-stem horse.
1138: Love does not stop to think whether someone is self-controlled or deserves pity. It breaks out of hiding and shows itself in the open street.
1139: As if it thinks not everyone knows about it yet, my love wanders confused through the streets.
1140: Thoughtless people laugh at me right in front of my eyes, only because they have never suffered what I suffer.
1141: Now that the town gossips about our love, my precious life, which was slipping away, holds on. Luckily, the gossips do not know their talk is what keeps me alive.
1142: This town does not know how rare and hard to win the girl with flower-like eyes is. By spreading a rumor about us, it has done me a favor.
1143: Isn't the rumor the whole town knows a gain for me? Hearing it, my heart feels as if we are already together, though we are not yet.
1144: My love grows and blooms because of the town's gossip. Without that gossip, it would lose its strength and shrink away.
1145: Just as a drinker wants more toddy (palm wine) each time it makes him happy, my love grows sweeter each time the rumor makes it known.
1146: I saw my love only once, yet the rumor has spread everywhere, like the news when the snake swallows the moon (an old way of describing an eclipse).
1147: This love-sickness grows like a crop. The town's gossip is its fertilizer, and my mother's angry words are its water.
1148: Thinking that gossip can put out love is like thinking you can put out a fire by pouring ghee (melted butter) on it.
1149: He once told me, 'Do not be afraid,' and now he has left me, shaming me in front of many. How can I still feel ashamed of the town's gossip?
1150: The town is now spreading the very rumor we wanted. So if we ask him, our lover will gladly agree to what we want.
1151: If you are not leaving, tell me so. But if your news is that you will go and hurry back, tell it to whoever is still alive when you return.
1152: Once, even his look was pure joy. Now even our hugs are full of pain, because I fear the parting that is coming.
1153: Even a wise and understanding lover leaves at some time. So it is hard to feel sure of anyone's promise never to leave.
1154: If the one who lovingly said 'Do not be afraid' goes away, is it the fault of the one who believed his comforting words?
1155: If you want to save me, stop my husband from going. Once he has left, being together again will be hard to get.
1156: If he is cruel enough to tell me to my face that he is leaving, then my hope that he will come back and be kind to me is a hope I can hardly hold on to.
1157: My bangles are slipping down my thin arm past the wrist. Surely they will tell the whole town that the lord of the seashore has left me.
1158: It is painful to live in a town where no one is close to you. It is even more painful to be apart from the one you love.
1159: Fire burns only when you touch it. Can fire, like love-sickness, burn you even when you move away from it?
1160: It seems many people can agree to the impossible, push away the pain, bear being apart, and still go on living afterwards.
1161: I would hide this pain of love from others, but like water in a spring that rises more the more you draw from it, it only grows the more I hide it.
1162: I cannot keep this love-pain hidden, and yet I feel too ashamed to tell it to the one who caused it.
1163: In my body, which cannot bear it any longer, love and shame hang from the two ends of a carrying pole. My very life is that pole.
1164: There is a sea of love in front of me, but there is no safe raft to cross it.
1165: If he can bring me such sadness while we are lovers, what would he do to me if he were my enemy?
1166: The joy of love is as big as the sea. But when love turns to pain, its sadness is even bigger than the sea.
1167: I swim the wild flood of love but see no shore. Even in the middle of the night, I am the only one awake.
1168: Poor night! It has put every living thing to sleep, and now it has no friend left but me.
1169: These long, slow nights are even crueler than the cruel man who left me.
1170: If my eyes could travel to where he is, the way my heart does, they would not have to swim in this flood of tears.
1171: This endless love-sickness came only because my eyes showed him to me. So why do those same eyes now cry and beg to see him?
1172: My dark-lined eyes looked at him back then without thinking about what would follow. Why do they suffer now, not seeing that they caused this sadness themselves?
1173: These eyes rushed on their own to look at him, and now they cry on their own. Surely that is something to laugh at.
1174: My lovely eyes planted in me a sickness I cannot escape or survive. Now they have cried so much that their tears have dried up.
1175: My eyes brought on a love-sickness bigger than the sea. Now they suffer the pain of not being able to sleep.
1176: Oh, how sweet this is! The eyes that gave me this sickness have now fallen into the same suffering themselves.
1177: My eyes once looked at him with melting, eager longing. Now let them ache and ache until every tear in them is gone.
1178: There is someone who loved me without truly caring for me. And yet my eyes cannot rest without seeing him.
1179: When he does not come, my eyes cannot sleep, and when he comes, they still cannot sleep. Either way, they suffer terrible pain.
1180: Townspeople easily learn the secret in the hearts of women like me, because our eyes announce it like a beaten drum.
1181: I myself agreed to let my loving husband go away. Now that my body has turned pale with longing, who else can I complain to?
1182: Proud that he gave it to me, this paleness climbs all over my body and spreads as if it owned it.
1183: He took away my beauty and my shyness. In return, he gave me love-sickness and this paleness.
1184: I think only of him and speak only of his goodness, yet the paleness has come anyway. Isn't that a trick?
1185: Look there, my lover is walking away. And look here, the paleness is already spreading over my body.
1186: Just as darkness waits for a lamp to go out, the paleness waits for the moment my husband's hug loosens.
1187: I lay held close in his arms. I turned away just a little, and in that instant the paleness rushed over me as if scooping me up.
1188: People only say, 'She has turned pale.' No one says, 'He has left her.'
1189: If the man who sweetly talked me into letting him go is doing well and is thought well of, then let my body turn as pale as it wants.
1190: I don't mind being called 'the pale one,' as long as people do not blame the man who talked me into letting him go for being unkind.
1191: Those who are loved back by the very one they love have won love's best prize. It is like a fruit with no hard seed inside, all sweetness.
1192: The kindness a lover shows to the one who loves him is like rain from the sky to those whose lives depend on it.
1193: Only a woman truly loved by the one she loves can proudly say, 'We will live happily again,' even while he is away.
1194: Even a woman admired by everyone is truly unlucky if the one she loves does not love her back.
1195: If the one I love does not love me back, what good can he possibly do for me?
1196: Love on one side only is painful. Like the load on a carrying pole, it is sweet only when it is balanced at both ends.
1197: Kaman, the god of love, works on only one side. Does he not see the pain and sadness he leaves in me?
1198: No one in the world is as hard-hearted, or as brave, as a woman who keeps on living without even one kind word from the one she loves.
1199: Even if the one I long for shows me no kindness, every word about him, even his name, is still sweet to my ears.
1200: Bless you, my heart! Telling your great pain to someone who does not care about you is like trying to fill up the sea.
